questions.question: Discuss the advantages and disadvantages of steaming as a cooking method.
questions.solution_html:
• =1, 2=2, 3=2]
  • Ans: Steaming – definition, applications
  • Advantages
  • • It preserves the main nutrients - As there is no direct contact with water, the
  • nutritional substances in food are not lost. Food therefore retains its nutrients
  • much better.
  • • Full and genuine flavour - Steamed foods retain their own genuine flavour
  • allowing us, in a certain sense, to “rediscover” their real essence. This cooking
  • method is ideal for fish and vegetables in particular.
  • • Less chance of burning and scorching.
  • • Texture of food is better as it becomes light and fluffy.
  • • Almost no smells - In most cases, steam cooking reduces the unpleasant
  • smells typical of some foods.
  • • Cooking time is less and fuel wastage is less.
  • • Steamed foods like idli and idiappam contain less fat and are easily digested
  • and are good for children, aged and for therapeutic diets.
  • • Nutrient loss is minimised.
  • • Quick and inexpensive .
  • Disadvantages
  • • Steamed vegetables can taste bland: addition of seasonings can overcome this
  • blandness.
  • • Constant attention is needed to avoid overcooking.
  • • Steamers use a lot of water.
  • • Steaming equipment is required.
  • • This method is limited to the preparation of selected foods..
questions.final_answer: • This method is limited to the preparation of selected foods

questions.question: How do the choice and availability of ingredients impact the authenticity of a dish in different regions?
questions.solution_html:
• Ingredient availability plays a major role in determining how authentic a dish remains when prepared in different
  • regions. Traditional dishes are deeply tied to local crops, climate, soil conditions, and cultural farming practices. When
  • certain indigenous ingredients are not available, cooks often substitute them with locally accessible items, which may
  • alter the original taste, flavour, aroma, and texture. For example, replacing Indian spices with milder ones in Western
  • countries can reduce the authenticity of curries. Similarly, tropical ingredients like coconut, tamarind, or certain
  • millets may have no exact substitutes, resulting in modified versions of the dish. While adaptation makes a dish
  • suitable for local taste, authenticity may be compromised because the original sensory experience, cultural
  • significance, and traditional methods rely heavily on the native ingredients..
questions.final_answer: significance, and traditional methods rely heavily on the native ingredients
questions.source_exam: First Semester MGU-UGP/MGU-BBA/MGU-BCA Honours Examinations November 2025

questions.question: How does the preparation of food during Vishu reflect Kerala’s agricultural heritage?
questions.solution_html:
• Vishu celebrations strongly highlight Kerala’s agricultural richness and seasonal abundance. The festival
  • marks the beginning of the agricultural year, and the Vishukani includes freshly harvested produce such as rice
  • coconut, cucumber, jackfruit, mangoes, and vegetables—symbolizing prosperity. Vishusadhya dishes are prepared
  • using seasonal ingredients, reflecting Kerala’s dependence on its fertile soil and monsoon-driven farming. The use of
  • fresh vegetables like ash gourd, pumpkin, and plantain signifies the diversity of Kerala’s crops. Rice, which is a staple
  • of Kerala agriculture, appears in multiple forms such as Vishu kanji and payasam. Thus, Vishu food traditions
  • reinforce Kerala’s strong agricultural identity and gratitude for natural abundance.
questions.final_answer: reinforce Kerala’s strong agricultural identity and gratitude for natural abundance
questions.source_exam: First Semester MGU-UGP/MGU-BBA/MGU-BCA Honours Examinations November 2025

questions.question: Write a brief note on globalization and food trade.
questions.solution_html:
• Globalization has significantly transformed food production, distribution, and consumption. Through global
  • trade networks, ingredients that were once confined to specific geographical regions are now available worldwide.
  • This enables the spread of culinary practices and fusion cuisines, contributing to cultural exchange. International food
  • corporations, improved transportation, and cold-chain storage have expanded markets for spices, grains, fruits, and
  • processed foods. However, globalization also leads to certain challenges: traditional food systems may weaken, local
  • cuisines may become homogenized, and small farmers may face economic pressure. Despite this, global food trade has
  • made diets more diverse, increased accessibility to exotic ingredients, and facilitated the exchange of culinary
  • knowledge between cultures..
questions.source_exam: First Semester MGU-UGP/MGU-BBA/MGU-BCA Honours Examinations November 2025

questions.question: Illustrate how ancient civilizations like the Greeks or Romans shaped modern culinary traditions?
questions.solution_html:
• Ancient Greek and Roman civilizations made several contributions that continue to influence modern cooking.
  • The Greeks developed early concepts of balanced diets, olive oil usage, and wine culture, which remain central to
  • Mediterranean cuisine today. They introduced herbs like oregano, thyme, and basil, and emphasized the combination
  • of grains, fruits, and vegetables in daily meals. Romans expanded these ideas and introduced innovations such as
  • advanced bread-making techniques, preserved foods, sauces like garum (a precursor to modern fish sauces), and
  • sophisticated banquet culture. Roman trade routes also helped spread spices, wheat, and olives across Europe. Many
  • modern European dishes, including pasta variations, sauces, and baked goods, trace their origins to these civilizations.
questions.final_answer: modern European dishes, including pasta variations, sauces, and baked goods, trace their origins to these civilizations
questions.source_exam: First Semester MGU-UGP/MGU-BBA/MGU-BCA Honours Examinations November 2025

questions.question: What are some iconic Christmas dishes in different parts of the world?
questions.solution_html:
• Christmas celebrations worldwide feature unique dishes reflecting each region’s culture and food habits. In the United
  • States and the UK, roast turkey or roast beef with mashed potatoes and gravy is common. Germany is known for
  • Stollen, a rich fruit cake dusted with sugar. In Italy, families enjoy dishes like Panettone and Feast of the Seven Fishes.
  • Mexico celebrates with Tamales and Pozole, while the Philippines features Lechon (roast pig) and Bibingka (rice
  • cake). In Australia, Christmas meals often include cold seafood like prawns because it falls in summer. These dishes
  • highlight how Christmas food traditions vary globally, blending local ingredients with Christian festive customs.
questions.final_answer: highlight how Christmas food traditions vary globally, blending local ingredients with Christian festive customs
questions.source_exam: First Semester MGU-UGP/MGU-BBA/MGU-BCA Honours Examinations November 2025

questions.question: What role does freshly harvested rice play in Pongal celebrations?
questions.solution_html:
• Freshly harvested rice is the centerpiece of Pongal celebrations, symbolizing abundance, prosperity, and gratitude for a
  • successful harvest. The festival is dedicated to the Sun God, thanking him for agricultural prosperity. Using newly
  • harvested rice signifies new beginnings and the hope of a fruitful year. The dish “Pongal,” cooked in a new clay pot
  • with fresh rice, milk, and jaggery, represents the overflowing of wealth and happiness. The first grains of the harvest
  • are believed to bring blessings to the household. Thus, freshly harvested rice reflects both agricultural significance and
  • deep cultural symbolism in Pongal traditions.
questions.final_answer: deep cultural symbolism in Pongal traditions
questions.source_exam: First Semester MGU-UGP/MGU-BBA/MGU-BCA Honours Examinations November 2025

questions.question: How do the choice and availability of ingredients impact the authenticity of a dish in different regions?
questions.solution_html:
• Ingredient availability plays a major role in determining how authentic a dish remains when prepared in different
  • regions. Traditional dishes are deeply tied to local crops, climate, soil conditions, and cultural farming practices. When
  • certain indigenous ingredients are not available, cooks often substitute them with locally accessible items, which may
  • alter the original taste, flavour, aroma, and texture. For example, replacing Indian spices with milder ones in Western
  • countries can reduce the authenticity of curries. Similarly, tropical ingredients like coconut, tamarind, or certain
  • millets may have no exact substitutes, resulting in modified versions of the dish. While adaptation makes a dish
  • suitable for local taste, authenticity may be compromised because the original sensory experience, cultural
  • significance, and traditional methods rely heavily on the native ingredients..
questions.final_answer: significance, and traditional methods rely heavily on the native ingredients
questions.source_exam: First Semester MGU-UGP/MGU-BBA/MGU-BCA Honours Examinations November 2025

questions.question: How does the preparation of food during Vishu reflect Kerala’s agricultural heritage?
questions.solution_html:
• Vishu celebrations strongly highlight Kerala’s agricultural richness and seasonal abundance. The festival
  • marks the beginning of the agricultural year, and the Vishukani includes freshly harvested produce such as rice
  • coconut, cucumber, jackfruit, mangoes, and vegetables—symbolizing prosperity. Vishusadhya dishes are prepared
  • using seasonal ingredients, reflecting Kerala’s dependence on its fertile soil and monsoon-driven farming. The use of
  • fresh vegetables like ash gourd, pumpkin, and plantain signifies the diversity of Kerala’s crops. Rice, which is a staple
  • of Kerala agriculture, appears in multiple forms such as Vishu kanji and payasam. Thus, Vishu food traditions
  • reinforce Kerala’s strong agricultural identity and gratitude for natural abundance.
questions.final_answer: reinforce Kerala’s strong agricultural identity and gratitude for natural abundance
questions.source_exam: First Semester MGU-UGP/MGU-BBA/MGU-BCA Honours Examinations November 2025

questions.question: Write a brief note on globalization and food trade.
questions.solution_html:
• Globalization has significantly transformed food production, distribution, and consumption. Through global
  • trade networks, ingredients that were once confined to specific geographical regions are now available worldwide.
  • This enables the spread of culinary practices and fusion cuisines, contributing to cultural exchange. International food
  • corporations, improved transportation, and cold-chain storage have expanded markets for spices, grains, fruits, and
  • processed foods. However, globalization also leads to certain challenges: traditional food systems may weaken, local
  • cuisines may become homogenized, and small farmers may face economic pressure. Despite this, global food trade has
  • made diets more diverse, increased accessibility to exotic ingredients, and facilitated the exchange of culinary
  • knowledge between cultures..
questions.source_exam: First Semester MGU-UGP/MGU-BBA/MGU-BCA Honours Examinations November 2025

questions.question: Illustrate how ancient civilizations like the Greeks or Romans shaped modern culinary traditions?
questions.solution_html:
• Ancient Greek and Roman civilizations made several contributions that continue to influence modern cooking.
  • The Greeks developed early concepts of balanced diets, olive oil usage, and wine culture, which remain central to
  • Mediterranean cuisine today. They introduced herbs like oregano, thyme, and basil, and emphasized the combination
  • of grains, fruits, and vegetables in daily meals. Romans expanded these ideas and introduced innovations such as
  • advanced bread-making techniques, preserved foods, sauces like garum (a precursor to modern fish sauces), and
  • sophisticated banquet culture. Roman trade routes also helped spread spices, wheat, and olives across Europe. Many
  • modern European dishes, including pasta variations, sauces, and baked goods, trace their origins to these civilizations.
questions.final_answer: modern European dishes, including pasta variations, sauces, and baked goods, trace their origins to these civilizations
questions.source_exam: First Semester MGU-UGP/MGU-BBA/MGU-BCA Honours Examinations November 2025

questions.question: What are some iconic Christmas dishes in different parts of the world?
questions.solution_html:
• Christmas celebrations worldwide feature unique dishes reflecting each region’s culture and food habits. In the United
  • States and the UK, roast turkey or roast beef with mashed potatoes and gravy is common. Germany is known for
  • Stollen, a rich fruit cake dusted with sugar. In Italy, families enjoy dishes like Panettone and Feast of the Seven Fishes.
  • Mexico celebrates with Tamales and Pozole, while the Philippines features Lechon (roast pig) and Bibingka (rice
  • cake). In Australia, Christmas meals often include cold seafood like prawns because it falls in summer. These dishes
  • highlight how Christmas food traditions vary globally, blending local ingredients with Christian festive customs.
questions.final_answer: highlight how Christmas food traditions vary globally, blending local ingredients with Christian festive customs

questions.question: What role does freshly harvested rice play in Pongal celebrations?
questions.solution_html:
• Freshly harvested rice is the centerpiece of Pongal celebrations, symbolizing abundance, prosperity, and gratitude for a
  • successful harvest. The festival is dedicated to the Sun God, thanking him for agricultural prosperity. Using newly
  • harvested rice signifies new beginnings and the hope of a fruitful year. The dish “Pongal,” cooked in a new clay pot
  • with fresh rice, milk, and jaggery, represents the overflowing of wealth and happiness. The first grains of the harvest
  • are believed to bring blessings to the household. Thus, freshly harvested rice reflects both agricultural significance and
  • deep cultural symbolism in Pongal traditions.
questions.final_answer: deep cultural symbolism in Pongal traditions
